explain.say: India has two great epics, the Ramayana and the Mahabharata: very long story poems in Sanskrit, told and retold for more than two thousand years. In India they are called itihasa, which means so it was.

b: A royal family split in two

explain.say: The Ramayana follows Prince Rama, who is sent away from his kingdom of Ayodhya for 14 years. His wife Sita and brother Lakshmana go with him, until the demon king Ravana carries Sita off to his island of Lanka.

Like many great stories, it climbs a story mountain. With the help of the brave Hanuman and an army of monkeys and bears, Rama crosses to Lanka, wins the battle, frees Sita and comes home to be crowned.

explain.say: The Mahabharata is about two sets of cousins. The five Pandava brothers, Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula and Sahadeva, are cheated out of their kingdom by their hundred cousins, the Kauravas, and the quarrel ends in a great war at Kurukshetra.

draw.text: Before the war, Krishna teaches Arjuna the Bhagavad Gita

explain.say: The Mahabharata is famous for stories within stories, like a set of nesting boxes. One storyteller tells it to a king, another retells it to sages in a forest, and inside are many more tales, such as Savitri, who outwits Yama, the lord of death.

items: Vaishampayana tells it to King Janamejaya
Ugrashravas retells it to sages in a forest
Inside: Savitri, Nala and Damayanti, the Gita

draw.text: A frame story holds other stories inside it

explain.say: The epics are still told everywhere: in village plays called Ramlila, shadow puppets in Indonesia, comics, novels, films and famous television series. They are great literature, and for many Hindus they are also sacred stories.

items: Ancient times: sung by bards and storytellers
1500s: Tulsidas retells the Ramayana in Hindi verse
1987 and 1988: Ramayan and Mahabharat on Indian TV
Today: Ramlila plays, shadow puppets, novels and films

faq.a: The Pandavas are the five heroic brothers of the Mahabharata: Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, and the twins Nakula and Sahadeva. They are the sons of King Pandu, and they fight their hundred cousins, the Kauravas, in the war of Kurukshetra.
asks: Who were the five brothers in the Mahabharata?

faq.a: The Ramayana tells how Prince Rama is sent into the forest for 14 years with his wife Sita and brother Lakshmana. When Ravana, king of Lanka, carries Sita away, Rama, helped by Hanuman, rescues her and returns home to be crowned king.
asks: Tell me the story of Rama and Sita
What is the Ramayana story for kids?

faq.a: The Mahabharata is the story of a royal family split in two. The five Pandava brothers are cheated out of their kingdom in a game of dice by their cousins, the Kauravas, and after years in exile the quarrel becomes a great 18 day war.
asks: Tell me the story of the Mahabharata

faq.q: How are the Ramayana and the Mahabharata different?
faq.a: The Ramayana is shorter, about 24,000 verses, and follows one hero, Rama, in a clear struggle of good against evil. The Mahabharata is about four times longer, follows a whole family, and shows heroes facing hard choices where right and wrong are not simple.
asks: What is the difference between the Ramayana and the Mahabharata?

faq.q: Which is older, the Ramayana or the Mahabharata?
faq.a: Hindu tradition places Rama's story in an earlier age than the Mahabharata, and the Mahabharata even retells a short version of the Ramayana. Scholars think both poems grew over many centuries, at overlapping times, so it is hard to say which came first.
asks: Did the Ramayana come before the Mahabharata?
When were the Indian epics written?

faq.a: An epic is a very long story poem about heroes, great journeys and battles, often with gods taking part. The Ramayana and Mahabharata are epics, like the Iliad and the Odyssey of ancient Greece.
asks: What does epic mean in literature?

faq.a: Hanuman is the brave and loyal hero of the monkey people in the Ramayana. He leaps across the sea to find Sita in Lanka and helps Rama win her back, and many Hindus worship him for his strength and devotion.
asks: Who is the monkey hero in the Ramayana?

faq.q: Who is Krishna in the Mahabharata?
faq.a: Krishna is the cousin and friend of the Pandavas, a wise prince who tries to make peace. In the war he drives Arjuna's chariot and teaches him the Bhagavad Gita, and many Hindus honour him as a form of the god Vishnu.
asks: What does Krishna do in the Mahabharata?

faq.q: Who are the main characters of the Ramayana?
faq.a: The main characters are Prince Rama; his wife Sita; his loyal brother Lakshmana; Hanuman, the monkey hero; and Ravana, the ten headed king of Lanka. Rama's brother Bharata and the monkey king Sugriva also play big parts.

faq.q: What are stories within stories in the Mahabharata?
faq.a: The Mahabharata is told by one storyteller to a king, then retold by another to sages in a forest, and inside it characters tell many more tales, such as Savitri and Nala and Damayanti. This is called a frame story, like nesting boxes.
asks: What is the story of Savitri?

faq.q: Are the Ramayana and Mahabharata religious books?
faq.a: They are both great works of literature and, for many Hindus, sacred stories. Rama and Krishna are honoured as forms of the god Vishnu, and the Bhagavad Gita, a key Hindu scripture, is part of the Mahabharata.
asks: Are the Ramayana and Mahabharata Hindu scriptures?

faq.q: How are the Ramayana and Mahabharata told today?
faq.a: They are acted in village plays such as the Ramlila, performed with shadow puppets in Indonesia, drawn in comics, written as novels and filmed. The Indian TV series Ramayan, from 1987, and Mahabharat, from 1988, were watched by huge audiences.
asks: Are there movies of the Ramayana?
How do people tell the epics now?

faq.q: Who are the rivals in the epics?
faq.a: In the Ramayana the rival is Ravana, king of Lanka, who carries off Sita. In the Mahabharata it is Duryodhana, eldest of the Kauravas. Both epics give their rivals real strengths too: Ravana is learned, and Duryodhana is a loyal friend to Karna.
asks: Who is the villain of the Ramayana?
Who is the villain of the Mahabharata?

facts: The Ramayana has about 24,000 verses in seven books and is traditionally by Valmiki.
The Mahabharata has about 100,000 couplets in its longest form, in 18 books, and is traditionally by Vyasa.
The five Pandavas are Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula and Sahadeva.
The Bhagavad Gita is part of the Mahabharata.
In India the two epics are called itihasa, which means so it was.

quiz.say: How many Pandava brothers are there in the Mahabharata?
quiz.show: How many Pandava brothers are there?
quiz.why: There are five Pandava brothers: Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula and Sahadeva.

wrong.0: 3 is too few; Arjuna is the third brother, but there are five.
wrong.2: 7 is the number of books in the Ramayana, not Pandava brothers.
wrong.3: 100 is the number of Kaurava brothers, the Pandavas' cousins.

quiz.say: On a story mountain, the climax is the most exciting, tense moment. Which part of the Ramayana is the climax?
quiz.show: Which part of the Ramayana is the climax?
quiz.why: The battle in Lanka is the moment of greatest tension, when the conflict between Rama and Ravana is decided.

wrong.1: Leaving Ayodhya starts the problem; it is the beginning of the rising action.
wrong.2: The crowning is the resolution, when everything is settled at the end.

quiz.say: The Ramayana and Mahabharata are more than two thousand years old, yet they are still told in comics, plays and films. Why do you think they last?
quiz.show: Why are the epics still retold today?

options.show: Their themes still matter to people
options.say: Their themes of family, courage, loyalty and right and wrong still matter
Nobody has written any new stories

quiz.why: The epics deal with questions everyone faces, like loyalty, courage, family quarrels and doing the right thing, so each generation finds them meaningful.

wrong.1: New stories are written all the time; the epics last because of their themes.
wrong.2: They are among the longest poems ever composed.
